text.p: These are the leading stories in Zambia's newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and can not vouch for their accuracy.

- The European Union said it hopes Zambia will have free and fair elections, conducted in a manner acceptable to all players, including former president Kenneth Kaunda's opposition party. In a declaration released in Lusaka on Monday, the EU said it would closely monitor the November 18 polls.
- Scores of people were injured in Lusaka on Monday when opposition cadres clashed with government supporters over the ownership of party offices in a high density township.

- The World Bank has commended Zambia for creating conditions for sustainable economic development. Vice-president of the bank for the African region, Callisto Mandavo, said before a meeting with finance minister Ronald Penza, that Zambia was leading the way for economic development in Africa.
- Home affairs minister Chitalu Sampa said on Monday that police would use force against law breakers in the run-up to the November 18 general elections.

- The paramount chief of Eastern Province, Mpezeni, on Monday urged president Frederick Chiluba to address people's concerns on the inadequacies of the voters register. He suggested that people excluded from the register be allowed to use their nationl registration cards to cast their ballots.
- There are more than 16,000 ghost voters in the voters register for Copperbelt Province, an examination of the register has disclosed.
